### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/trigger-api`, `@objectstack/trigger-schedule`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via flowName (literal, a string literal in start), hookId (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via flowName (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), flowName (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via flowName (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via flowName (literal, a string literal in start))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51922976b4f8aa1ad3feb36fcdf22da31f29e767` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `385cab8a36a4f939e9708b1ff9548378864fc3b5` — the merge of head `95d9b479fa71d837a8f09e5a4881edca6d24094c` into base `51922976b4f8aa1ad3feb36fcdf22da31f29e767`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 385cab8a36a4f939e9708b1ff9548378864fc3b5 && git checkout 385cab8a36a4f939e9708b1ff9548378864fc3b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 51922976b4f8aa1ad3feb36fcdf22da31f29e767 95d9b479fa71d837a8f09e5a4881edca6d24094c && git checkout -B drift-repro 51922976b4f8aa1ad3feb36fcdf22da31f29e767 && git merge --no-ff 95d9b479fa71d837a8f09e5a4881edca6d24094c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51922976b4f8aa1ad3feb36fcdf22da31f29e767
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 51922976b4f8aa1ad3feb36fcdf22da31f29e767` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4163e675debec1e21865a16b329b1aed4c249ac4`
Local-runs: none

The declaration face: the committed changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and no path of the 16 hits the governed register (`check-governed-merges --pr 32374`: 0 of 16, 1398 lines). Read on the diff `b2c0202f...4163e675`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Arming.** `activateFlowTrigger` now arms each slot of a name two packages hold under its key; main declined every such slot (`isSharedFlowKey`). Only the M1 lone-shared slot (the registry holds the name twice, one body refused) stays declined, because it still holds the bare key. One-holder names reach the same `execute(flowName)` path as before through `triggerRun`, whose first branch is `execute(armedKey)` when no slot moved.
- **Fire.** `triggerRun(armedKey)` captures the slot at arm time and resolves its current key at fire time. A key that moved while the old binding is released runs nothing and returns `undefined`; the caller now returns early on `undefined`, so no failure is logged for a dropped stale event. A shared slot runs through `executeKey` with `params.flowName` rewritten from the key to the flow's name only when the trigger seeded it with the key.
- **Dispatch keys.** `flowDispatchHolder` answers a slot-key spelling with `{ packageId, claimBare: false, name }`. Both schedule triggers spell the key with `holder.name ?? flowName`, so a one-holder name (no `name` member) keys exactly as before, and a slot keys as `schedule:PACKAGE:NAME:WINDOW`, the key it claimed while it held the name alone.
- **Inbound hook.** `inboundHookSlot` answers `undefined` for every name that is no slot key and that no two packages hold, and both faces then take main's path unchanged (the bare mount serves the name; the qualified route asks `admitInboundHookAddress` with the same namespace owners, read once now instead of inside the predicate). A slot-key spelling or an unfiled key is `unadmitted`; a qualified shared name is `served` only when exactly one slot's package is owned by the namespace (`_env`: the slot with no package). The bare hook of a shared name gets `refuseSharedName`, which goes through `refuseUnverified`: the same 401 bytes as every unverified post, after the body is read, with `shared-name` and the holders in the log only. That holds the inbound-door rule that the anonymous answer never says whether a flow exists or which packages hold it.
- **Member.** `handleInboundHook` refuses a name carrying `/` as an unknown flow. On main no hook could be armed under such a name (a shared slot was never armed, and a one-holder flow binds under its bare name), so the answer a post gets is the same 401.
- **Hosted face.** The qualified route serves a routed slot only through `handleInboundSlotHook`; a slot answer with no slot door, and any unadmitted address, takes `refuseUnaddressed`, which is main's refusal block moved into a function (same log line, same `inboundHookRefusalResponse`). The bare route still reads no service before the member.

### ② Semver level

Patch on `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/trigger-api`, `@objectstack/trigger-schedule` and `@objectstack/runtime`, matching the changeset. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no authorable key is added, removed or reshaped; the new names are engine and trigger door methods and an optional member on two structural interfaces. ADR-0087 `not-required` holds: nothing a migration could rewrite.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds. Every answer a caller could already get is unchanged: one-holder bindings, job names, dispatch keys and hook answers are each pinned by a CONTROL; the shared-name hook paths answered 401 on main and answer the same 401 bytes now. What is added is that shared-name slots are armed and reached by their qualified hook.
- No narrowing found. The only newly refused input (a `/` name at the member) had no armed hook to reach on main.
- Carried, not owed here: the `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` inbound-hook line and the `subflow` parenthetical ride PR-3 (a skills path would make this PR Tier H). The `disablePackage` holder finding in ruling 5 is outside this PR and recorded on the card.
- Nit, no effect: the `@objectstack/core` import in `automation-hooks.ts` is reflowed onto several lines with no change.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-qtot7s`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzg5AUtn9pwa3g2bBqk`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**Epic red-line read — PASS at `4163e675`** (#31696 PR-2: triggers and the inbound hook by slot) · 2026-11-11T05:42Z

The epic seat stood down before this head; this session took the epic seat over at the maintainer's request to follow finished PRs to merge. I read the diff `b2c0202f...4163e675` (16 files) and the cited engine code, and did not run it. CI on this head: 56 check-runs, 38 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed. Contract review (declaration face) is 6783963300, PASS.

**Red line 1 — resolution is never loosened.**
- A trigger arms each slot of a shared name under its own key, and `triggerRun` captures the slot at arm time and fires `executeKey(key)` for that slot. It never re-resolves the bare name at fire time. A slot whose key moved and whose old binding was released runs nothing (`undefined`), and the caller now returns early on it.
- The M1 lone-shared slot (a second holder's body refused) stays declined: `loneSharedFlowKey(...) === flowName`, behind the warning.
- `inboundHookSlot` serves a qualified hook only when exactly one slot matches: `_env` only the package-less slot; a namespace only a slot whose package is among the namespace's owners **and** whose loader set ships it (`packagedFlowOwner(key) === slot.packageId`). Anything else is `unadmitted`. A slot key or a `\u0000` name in the name position is `unadmitted` on both mounts and both faces (the member's own `/` fallback covers an engine without `inboundHookSlot`).
- The hosted face refuses a routed slot when the member has no slot door, never serving it by name.

**Red line 2 — ambiguity is reported, never guessed.**
- The bare hook of a name two packages hold picks neither flow. It answers the door's one 401 and logs `shared-name` with every holder; nothing is enqueued (dogfood `flow-hook-per-slot` pins 401, the log line and no run).
- D5 names a `409` naming the holders. Withholding that on this anonymous door is accepted, as the seat ruled at 00:25Z on #31696: the door's answer never says whether a flow name exists or which packages are installed (G1's unadmitted-address precedent), and the server log carries the report. Carrier, not owed here: the ADR-0150 amendment card #32362 should carry one sentence that D5's `409` does not apply to the inbound hook door.

**Red line 3 — independently releasable.**
- A name one package holds keeps its bare binding and runs through `execute(name)` as before (the CONTROL pins; dogfood "a name one package holds is served by its bare hook, as before").
- Schedule job ids stay `flow-schedule:NAME` for one holder. A slot's dispatch key is `schedule:PACKAGE:NAME:WINDOW`, the key the same slot claimed while it held the name alone, so a re-arm window is claimed once. The package-less slot keeps the bare key, distinct from a package slot.
- Additive only: an optional `name` member on two structural interfaces, a new engine method and a new member door off the contract. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with the ADR-0087 not-required marker.

**Before landing:** main is 28 first-parent commits past the merge base (K ≥ 15), so a main merge comes first. A trial merge is textually clean and leaves the PR's diff against main identical (16 files, +1319 −79); the only engine change on main since the base is #32257's script-node hunk, which this diff does not touch. This read carries over a merge-only head move; any other move needs a re-read.

All three red lines hold. Contract review, ACCEPT and landing belong to the lane seat.
